title: Rendering Keywords: From Scene Representation to Display Output
abstract: Thirty-four rendering keyword groups, from scene creation to display presentation, with three primary or official sources attached to every keyword.
image: /content/blog/Rendering Keywords - From Scene Representation to Display Output/rendering-keywords.svg
imageAlt: Thirty-four rendering topics arranged across scene creation, visibility, light transport, and display output
lede: This source guide preserves the supplied 30-part rendering vocabulary exactly and adds focused sections on hair, fog, water, and particle lighting. Under every keyword, it provides three links to primary research, normative specifications, or official implementation documentation.

sections.heading: Scene graph and asset interchange
paragraphs: OpenUSD, USD Stage, Prim, layers, composition arcs, references, payloads, variants, instancing, glTF, FBX, OBJ.

USD is especially relevant for large production scenes because it describes how assets are assembled and overridden, rather than merely storing one mesh. [OpenUSD concepts](https://openusd.org/release/glossary.html), [glTF 2.0 specification](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html)

sections.heading: Geometry representation
paragraphs: Mesh primitives, triangle topology, vertex buffer, index buffer, vertex attributes, normals, tangents, vertex colors, skinning, morph targets, procedural geometry.

sections.heading: Textures and material assets
paragraphs: UV mapping, texels, texture samplers, mipmaps, texture filtering, normal maps, displacement maps, texture compression, channel packing, material graphs, shader graphs.

sections.heading: Large-world and terrain representation
paragraphs: Heightfield, heightmap, weightmap, terrain tiles, quadtree, geometry clipmaps, continuous geo-mipmapping, LOD, HLOD, world partition, geometry streaming, virtual texturing, runtime virtual textures.
Modern large-world systems combine geometry LOD with streaming and partitioning. [Unreal Engine Landscape overview](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/landscape-overview)

sections.heading: Modern alternative scene representations
paragraphs: Point cloud, voxel, signed distance field, surfel, neural radiance field, NeRF, radiance field, 3D Gaussian Splatting, splat rasterization, differentiable rendering, novel-view synthesis.

3DGS should be presented as a learned scene representation and visibility-aware splatting method, not as an ordinary mesh file format. [Original 3D Gaussian Splatting paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3592433)

sections.heading: Coordinate spaces
paragraphs: Object space, local space, world space, view space, eye space, clip space, normalized device coordinates, NDC, screen space, viewport space, framebuffer coordinates.

sections.heading: Camera and projection
paragraphs: Model matrix, view matrix, projection matrix, model-view-projection matrix, MVP, homogeneous coordinates, perspective projection, orthographic projection, field of view, aspect ratio, near plane, far plane, perspective divide, viewport transform, reverse-Z.

sections.heading: Programmable geometry pipeline
paragraphs: Vertex shader, primitive assembly, tessellation, geometry shader, amplification shader, task shader, mesh shader, meshlet, primitive shader.

Mesh shaders reorganize geometry into small meshlet batches and allow GPU-side primitive generation and culling. [DirectX Mesh Shader specification](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/MeshShader.html)

sections.heading: Culling and level of detail
paragraphs: Back-face culling, frustum culling, occlusion culling, hierarchical Z-buffer, Hi-Z, depth pyramid, LOD selection, HLOD, cluster culling, GPU-driven rendering, indirect drawing, virtualized geometry, Nanite.

Nanite is a useful modern case study because it uses hierarchical geometry clusters, streaming, and visibility-driven detail selection. [Nanite documentation](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/nanite-in-unreal-engine)

sections.heading: Rasterization and fragment generation
paragraphs: Primitive clipping, triangle setup, rasterization, coverage, fragment, sample, barycentric interpolation, perspective-correct interpolation, scissor test, depth test, stencil test, early-Z, blending, framebuffer, render target, MSAA.
Rasterization is the missing central stage in the original draft. [Vulkan rasterization specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/primsrast.html)

sections.heading: Ray traversal and visibility
paragraphs: Primary ray, shadow ray, secondary ray, ray–triangle intersection, acceleration structure, bounding-volume hierarchy, BVH, bottom-level acceleration structure, BLAS, top-level acceleration structure, TLAS, ray query, closest-hit shader, any-hit shader.
[DirectX Raytracing specification](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/Raytracing.html)

sections.heading: Radiometry and the rendering equation
paragraphs: Radiant flux, irradiance, radiance, solid angle, emitted radiance, incident radiance, outgoing radiance, rendering equation, light transport equation, local illumination, global illumination.

The rendering equation provides the mathematical center of the article: outgoing light combines emission with reflected incoming light. [PBRT light transport equation](https://www.pbr-book.org/4ed/Light_Transport_I_Surface_Reflection/The_Light_Transport_Equation)

sections.heading: Renderer organization
paragraphs: Forward rendering, deferred rendering, forward+, clustered forward shading, tiled shading, G-buffer, visibility buffer, material pass, lighting pass, render graph.

sections.heading: Physically based material models
paragraphs: PBR, BRDF, BSDF, BTDF, BSSRDF, BxDF, Lambert, microfacet model, GGX, Trowbridge–Reitz distribution, normal-distribution function, NDF, Fresnel term, Smith masking-shadowing, energy conservation.

sections.heading: Material parameters and specialized lobes
paragraphs: Base color, albedo, metallic, roughness, specular, normal, emissive, ambient occlusion, index of refraction, anisotropy, clearcoat, sheen, iridescence, transmission, thin-film interference, subsurface scattering, layered materials, hair shading.

Modern “principled” materials collect these behaviors into an artist-facing model. [Disney Principled BRDF](https://disneyanimation.com/publications/physically-based-shading-at-disney/), [Khronos physically based material parameters](https://registry.khronos.org/ANARI/specs/1.1/ANARI-1.1.html)

sections.heading: Hair rendering and lighting
paragraphs: Hair strands, hair cards, groom, fiber scattering, longitudinal roughness, azimuthal roughness, melanin absorption, primary highlight, secondary highlight, multiple scattering, deep opacity maps, hair transmittance, strand voxelization, hair self-shadowing.

Hair lighting is a fiber-transport problem rather than an ordinary surface BRDF. A production renderer must represent sub-pixel coverage, evaluate longitudinal and azimuthal scattering around each strand, model absorption through melanin or artist parameters, and preserve transmission and self-shadowing through a dense groom.

sections.heading: Direct lighting and light sampling
paragraphs: Directional light, point light, spot light, area light, environment light, emissive geometry, image-based lighting, IBL, importance sampling, multiple importance sampling, MIS, many-light sampling.

sections.heading: Shadow methods
paragraphs: Shadow map, percentage-closer filtering, PCF, PCSS, cascaded shadow maps, CSM, variance shadow maps, exponential variance shadow maps, EVSM, virtual shadow maps, ray-traced shadows, distance-field shadows, contact shadows.

“VSM” is ambiguous: it can mean Variance Shadow Maps or the newer Virtual Shadow Maps. The blog must spell out which one is intended. [Modern Unreal Engine shadow methods](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/shadowing-in-unreal-engine)

sections.heading: Global illumination and path sampling
paragraphs: Indirect illumination, diffuse bounce, glossy bounce, Monte Carlo integration, path tracing, bidirectional path tracing, Russian roulette, next-event estimation, ReSTIR DI, ReSTIR GI, reservoir sampling, spatiotemporal sample reuse.

ReSTIR extends the draft’s ray-tracing discussion with modern sample reuse for many lights and indirect paths. [ReSTIR DI](https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2020-07_spatiotemporal-reservoir-resampling-real-time-ray-tracing-dynamic-direct), [ReSTIR GI](https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2021-06_restir-gi-path-resampling-real-time-path-tracing)

sections.heading: Baked and cached lighting
paragraphs: Lightmap, baked global illumination, irradiance volume, light probe, reflection probe, radiance probe, irradiance cache, radiance cache, spherical harmonics, precomputed radiance transfer, PRT, radiosity, dynamic diffuse global illumination, DDGI, neural radiance cache, Lumen.
Spherical harmonics approximate low-frequency directional lighting; they do not store arbitrary lighting exactly.

sections.heading: Transparency and transmission
paragraphs: Alpha testing, alpha masking, alpha blending, sorted transparency, order-independent transparency, OIT, depth peeling, weighted blended OIT, refraction, Fresnel reflection, Beer–Lambert absorption, thickness, caustics.

sections.heading: Participating media, fog, smoke, and fire
paragraphs: Participating media, extinction, absorption, emission, in-scattering, out-scattering, scattering coefficient, phase function, Henyey–Greenstein phase function, transmittance, optical depth, single scattering, multiple scattering, ray marching, delta tracking, null scattering, froxel, voxel grid, sparse volume texture, OpenVDB.

Particle simulation and volume rendering should be separated: one determines how material moves, while the other determines how light travels through it. [PBRT volume scattering](https://www.pbr-book.org/4ed/Volume_Scattering)

sections.heading: Fog rendering and lighting
paragraphs: Fog density, extinction coefficient, single scattering, multiple scattering, phase function, anisotropy, transmittance, froxel grid, volumetric shadowing, light shafts, temporal reprojection, local fog volume, heterogeneous volume, sparse volume texture.

Fog becomes visible when participating media remove radiance along the view ray and add light scattered from the environment. Real-time systems usually discretize that transport into a camera-aligned froxel grid, inject light and shadow information, integrate toward the camera, and stabilize the low-resolution result with temporal reprojection.

sections.heading: Sky, atmosphere, and clouds
paragraphs: Rayleigh scattering, Mie scattering, ozone absorption, aerial perspective, atmospheric transmittance, sky-view LUT, transmittance LUT, precomputed atmosphere, volumetric cloud, cloud density, cloud ray marching, cloud shadowing.

[Physically based sky atmosphere](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sky-atmosphere-component-in-unreal-engine), [Volumetric cloud rendering](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/volumetric-cloud-component-in-unreal-engine)

sections.heading: Water rendering and simulation
paragraphs: Fresnel reflection, refraction, absorption, underwater scattering, surface normals, wave spectrum, FFT ocean, Gerstner waves, shallow-water equations, screen-space reflection, planar reflection, ray-traced reflection, caustics, foam, spray, SPH, FLIP simulation.
Water shading and water simulation should be separate subsections. A renderer can shade an animated wave surface without running a physically accurate fluid simulation.

sections.heading: Water surface and underwater lighting
paragraphs: Water BSDF, Fresnel reflection, Snell refraction, spectral absorption, volume scattering, phase function, surface normal spectrum, environment reflection, underwater lighting, refractive caustics, foam shading, single-layer water.

Water lighting couples a dielectric boundary to a participating medium. The surface selects reflected and refracted paths from its normal distribution, while the traveled distance below the surface controls absorption, in-scattering, underwater color, and the visibility of refractive caustics.

sections.heading: Particle rendering and lighting
paragraphs: Particle sprite, billboard, mesh particle, ribbon particle, GPU particle, particle material, soft particle, alpha blending, order-independent transparency, particle sorting, overdraw, lit translucency, particle self-shadowing, particle light, volumetric particle.

A particle simulation only supplies positions and attributes; a renderer still chooses a sprite, mesh, ribbon, light, or volumetric representation. Transparent particles then expose three separate costs: sorting or approximate compositing, repeated fragment work from overdraw, and low-resolution lighting or shadow structures for translucent media.

sections.heading: HDR buffers, exposure, and adaptation
paragraphs: Scene-linear HDR, floating-point render target, luminance, exposure value, EV, pre-exposure, auto exposure, luminance histogram, eye adaptation, local exposure.

sections.heading: Tone mapping and color management
paragraphs: Tone mapping, Reinhard operator, filmic tone mapping, ACES, scene-referred color, display-referred color, color grading, 3D LUT, white balance, gamut mapping, gamut compression.

ACES 2 separates its Output Transform into a rendering transform and display encoding, which is a useful distinction between choosing the image’s appearance and encoding it for a device. [ACES Output Transforms](https://docs.acescentral.com/system-components/output-transforms/)

sections.heading: Screen-space lighting approximations
paragraphs: SSAO, HBAO, GTAO, SSR, SSGI, screen-space shadows, depth pyramid, normal buffer, temporal accumulation, off-screen information loss.

sections.heading: Anti-aliasing and image reconstruction
paragraphs: Supersampling, SSAA, MSAA, FXAA, SMAA, TAA, TAAU, temporal jitter, motion vectors, reprojection, history rejection, disocclusion, dynamic resolution, temporal upscaling, TSR, FSR, XeSS, DLSS Super Resolution.

Modern temporal reconstruction uses information from multiple frames and therefore depends heavily on correct motion vectors. [Unreal Engine Temporal Super Resolution](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/temporal-super-resolution-in-unreal-engine)

sections.heading: Ray-tracing denoising and neural reconstruction
paragraphs: Spatial denoising, temporal denoising, variance estimation, sample accumulation, firefly removal, neural denoising, ray reconstruction, DLSS Ray Reconstruction, neural rendering.

sections.heading: Camera and lens effects
paragraphs: Bloom, convolution bloom, depth of field, circle of confusion, bokeh, motion blur, lens flare, vignette, chromatic aberration, film grain.

sections.heading: Display encoding and presentation
paragraphs: Linear RGB, sRGB, transfer function, OETF, EOTF, SDR, HDR10, PQ, HLG, display primaries, white point, bit depth, quantization, dithering, swapchain, presentation.

closing: These sources turn the original 30-part vocabulary and four new lighting sections into a research map: each keyword now has a direct path into the papers, specifications, and production documentation that define or implement it.
